A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussTR and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting a reliable comparison. Both contain 11 pages and end with references; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GaussTR evaluations on Occ3D-nuScenes, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and qualitative predictions in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original GaussTR evaluations, retaining earlier results and adding Talk2DINO-based results and ablations in Tables 1, 3 and 4.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Talk2DINO-aligned DINOv2 features as an alternative to MaskCLIP with FeatUp. This extends the feature extraction and alignment components while retaining the Gaussian Transformer, splatting, losses and similarity-based occupancy inference.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Occ3D-nuScenes six-camera driving data and semantic occupancy task. The qualitative open-vocabulary examples involving traffic lights and street signs are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 1 retain SelfOcc, OccNeRF, DistillNeRF and GaussianOcc as external comparators, with unchanged baseline scores. The added foundation-model configurations are variants within GaussTR's ablations.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated training schedule from 24 to 20 epochs and input resolution from 432 × 768 to 504 × 896. Tables 3–4 add Talk2DINO configurations with segmentation and query-count controls. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained FeatUp results were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 replaces the DINO/FeatUp local-feature study with comparisons of feature alignment and auxiliary segmentation, including Talk2DINO with and without segmentation. Table 4 extends query sensitivity to Talk2DINO. Together these substantially revise the analyses by testing backbone-dependent segmentation effects and scaling behavior; Table 2 retains its existing evidence under revised terminology.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The reporting practice remains single-valued results.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains augmented FeatUp's 45.19 IoU/11.70 mIoU and adds Talk2DINO's 44.54/12.27, replacing the unaugmented per-class row. Tables 3–4 add Talk2DINO results and remove the earlier DINO-combination results. The 400-query augmented FeatUp result changes from 44.27/11.23 to 44.65/11.52. Changed configurations and training settings prevent treating the headline increase as a controlled cross-version gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 retain the same Gaussian parameterization, transformations, PCA projections, rendering, losses and semantic inference. Changes to delta notation and summation notation do not substantively revise the mathematics; no theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The main claims of sparse, self-supervised, open-vocabulary occupancy prediction remain. The abstract, introduction and conclusion update the performance claim from 11.70 to 12.27 mIoU, while the claimed advantage over prior methods increases from approximately 18% to 23% and the training-time saving decreases from 50% to 40%.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds an optimization-conflict hypothesis for segmentation supervision harming Talk2DINO despite helping FeatUp. It also narrows the declining performance at high query counts to FeatUp and interprets Talk2DINO's continued improvement as evidence of richer representations. The existing limitations concerning small objects and occluded flat surfaces largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies depth-proportional scale and camera-relative rotation initialization, identifies the Talk2DINO backbone, and updates reported training time from approximately 10 to 12 hours on eight A800 GPUs. It removes the ViTDet feature-pyramid description and explicit 16× rendering downsampling detail. The code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Talk2DINO and the original Vision Transformer paper and removes the ViTDet citation accompanying the deleted feature-pyramid description. The broader positioning relative to occupancy prediction and generalizable Gaussian splatting remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, experimental discussion and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The ablation narrative is reorganized around feature alignment, and an acknowledgement is added. This is broad language revision despite retaining the overall section sequence.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 gain explicit backbone and segmentation columns, and Table 1 changes its GaussTR row labels. Figure 1 revises its vertical axis, including an axis break, and its caption. Other captions are edited, while the architecture illustration, qualitative image panels and overall layout remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded ablations better separate feature-alignment and segmentation effects and reveal useful backbone-dependent failure and scaling behavior. This provides a limited improvement in empirical support and interpretation. The gains are tempered by removed implementation details and a new reporting inconsistency: unaugmented FeatUp has 44.43 IoU in Table 3 but 44.73 in Table 4. Changed training settings also limit interpretation of the higher headline score.
